clue.text: Creature that's hit — a victim

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or strike hard
prey is a victim, something hunted

explanation.surface: An animal that has been struck turns out to be a casualty.
explanation.definitionFit: The lamprey is an eel-like jawless fish, a creature of rivers and seas.

clue.text: Fail to keep a card and go down

parts.note: to lose is to fail to keep
a heart is a playing card of one suit

explanation.surface: Someone drops a card and the game is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is to become dispirited, to sink in mood.

clue.text: Drink — manual worker wants a litre

parts.note: a miner does heavy work by hand

explanation.surface: A labourer is after a big bottle of something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'minerals' are fizzy soft drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A mineral, short for mineral water, is a carbonated soft drink in British usage.

clue.text: Sailors in two shades of blue…

parts.note: royal blue is one shade
navy blue is another shade

explanation.surface: Seamen are dressed in a pair of blue hues.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Navy is Britain's naval force, its seagoing service personnel.

clue.text: …follow up always a clue

annotationWithheld.why: '…follow up always a clue' (YARN): YA is always (AY) turned up, but the RN that follows comes from 'Sailors' in 3 down across the ellipsis, a word in another clue this format cannot quote

clue.text: Caretaker rising after New Year's Day

indicators.note: after places the word for a rising behind the date that precedes it

parts.note: New Year's Day is 1 January, written JAN I with a Roman numeral one
a rising is a hill, and a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A caretaker gets out of bed once the new year has begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reads as getting up but is a noun here: a tor is a high rocky hill on Dartmoor and similar moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor is a building's custodian, the person who looks after its upkeep.

clue.text: He ate with a finger bowl, the gardener, about 3

parts.note: the jack is the small target ball in the game of bowls

indicators.note: about puts the gardener around the abbreviation for the 3 down answer

parts.note: a hoer is one who hoes, a gardener
3 down is the Royal Navy, abbreviated RN

explanation.surface: A gardener who ate with his fingers is about to wash them in a bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme boy 'put in his thumb and pulled out a plum' from his Christmas pie.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Jack Horner, from the nursery rhyme, picked a plum out of his pie by hand.

clue.text: The present given finally and formerly

indicators.note: finally takes the final letter of given

parts.note: once means formerly, at one time

explanation.surface: A gift handed over at last, and at one time too.
explanation.walkthrough: Nonce is mostly met in 'for the nonce', meaning for now.
explanation.definitionFit: The nonce is the time being, the occasion at hand.

clue.text: The night before Epiphany, when the season opens

definitions.meaning: ... Night is 5 January, the eve of Epiphany
the Glorious ... is 12 August, start of the grouse-shooting season

explanation.surface: The eve of Epiphany, when the season begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Glorious Twelfth', 12 August, is when grouse shooting opens in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name a date, 5 January's eve and 12 August's opening day of shooting.

clue.text: Rustic sport winning the heart of Australians

indicators.note: winning means the sport gains the central letters that follow it

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union

indicators.note: the heart of means the central letters of Australians

explanation.surface: A country game takes the Aussies' fancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural means of the countryside, as a rustic thing is.

clue.text: Lad is 12, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for 12 is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: 12 refers to the answer at 12 across, meaning bright, i.e. sunny

explanation.surface: A boy is said to be twelve years old.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' is not an age but a cross-reference to 12 across, whose sense 'bright' gives SUNNY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonny is a familiar way to address a young boy.

clue.text: You want a different race to run — he'll give you 4

indicators.note: different asks for the letters of race to run in another order

explanation.surface: Someone after a change of event is told it will come with a story.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' is a cross-reference to 4 down, YARN, so the definition is a person who gives you a yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled storyteller, someone who spins tales for listeners.

clue.text: Kept artist imprisoned, in York, perhaps

indicators.note: imprisoned means the artist is locked up inside the word for kept

parts.note: kept means held
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter is held in jail in the city of York.
explanation.walkthrough: York is not the city but York Herald, one of the officers of arms of the College of Arms.
explanation.definitionFit: York Herald is a title in the English heraldic establishment, an example of an officer of arms.

clue.text: Bright companion given a verbal reprimand

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour

indicators.note: verbal signals that the reprimand word is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: an earful is a scolding

explanation.surface: A friend gets told off out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Verbal' looks like part of the telling-off, but it is the sound signal: an earful spoken aloud rhymes with the end of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright in the sense of happy and lively in mood, as a sunny disposition.

clue.text: Mechanism temp can see working

indicators.note: working suggests the letters of temp can see in action, rearranged

explanation.surface: An office temp gets to watch a machine running.
explanation.definitionFit: The escapement is the part of a clock or watch that regulates the release of power.

clue.text: 'ail from somewhere in Scotland

definitions.meaning: a hail or greeting, halloa, with its opening H dropped as the apostrophe in the clue shows
a town in Clackmannanshire on the Forth

explanation.surface: A greeting comes from a place north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: Halloa is an old form of hallo used to hail someone; drop the H, as the clue's 'ail does, and you have the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a Scottish town on the River Forth; halloa without its H is an h-dropped greeting call.

clue.text: Portable bed for Procrustes?

definitions.meaning: a carried frame for moving the sick or injured
the Greek bandit who racked guests to fit his bed, one who elongates people

explanation.surface: A carry-cot sized for the legendary host who made guests fit his bed.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Procrustes stretched short guests (and cut down tall ones) to fit his bed, so he was literally one who stretches.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical litter carries patients; Procrustes, who lengthened victims on his bed, is one who pulls things longer.

clue.text: Venture across desert

parts.note: a throw is a venture, a gamble
over means across

explanation.surface: Take a chance crossing arid country.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone over is to abandon them, to jilt or forsake.

clue.text: Remember about prayer

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a collect is a short liturgical prayer

explanation.surface: Bear in mind something concerning a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: To recollect is to recall something to mind.

clue.text: Cooked tacky pies and trifle

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of tacky pies being worked over into something new

explanation.surface: Sticky pies and a pudding have been baked.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipsy cake is a sponge soaked in wine or sherry, a dessert much like a trifle.

clue.text: City that rose from the ashes

definitions.meaning: the mythical bird reborn from its own ashes

explanation.surface: A town that was rebuilt after a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoenix is a US state capital and also the legendary bird reborn from its pyre.

clue.text: Mrs de Winter's not about to produce old instrument

indicators.note: not says the word for about must be left out of the name

parts.note: Rebecca is the first Mrs de Winter in Daphne du Maurier's novel Rebecca
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A novel's heroine is not near enough to make a period instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': Mrs de Winter is not 'about', so take CA out of REBECCA.
explanation.definitionFit: The rebec is a medieval bowed string instrument, an ancestor of the violin.

clue.text: Worker to mark the shortest route

parts.note: a worker is a type of bee
a line is a mark

explanation.surface: An employee is told to mark the quickest way.
explanation.definitionFit: A beeline is a direct course, as straight as a bee is said to fly home.

clue.text: .15 to see her in disarray

definitions.note: 15 refers to the answer at 15 across, a stretcher

indicators.note: in disarray means the letters of to see her are jumbled

explanation.surface: A stretcher is needed because she is in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: '15' points to 15 across, STRETCHER; the stray point before it is a printing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe tree is a device put inside footwear to keep it stretched to shape.

clue.text: Employees write notes on this

definitions.meaning: the people employed by an organisation
the five-line musical stave on which notes are written

explanation.surface: Workers take down notes on something.
explanation.definitionFit: Staff means personnel, and a musical staff (stave) holds written music.

clue.text: Conclusions in pamphlet for you are better, more correct

indicators.note: Conclusions in takes the last letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: The endings in a leaflet for you are an improvement, more accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: Truer is the comparative of true, meaning more accurate.

clue.text: From Warsaw he eloped like Daisy Bell

indicators.note: From signals the answer is taken out of the run of letters in Warsaw he eloped

explanation.surface: A man ran off from Poland's capital in a romantic flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy Bell is the music-hall song about 'a bicycle made for two'.
explanation.definitionFit: Awheel means riding a bicycle, as Daisy and her suitor do on their tandem.

clue.text: Sticks up for showing complacency

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the word for sticks reads from bottom to top

parts.note: gums means sticks, glues

explanation.surface: Someone stands up for a self-satisfied attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug describes someone excessively pleased with themselves.

clue.text: A man used a movement sickeningly

indicators.note: movement means the letters of a man used a are shifted around

explanation.surface: Someone has put one movement of a piece to tiresome use.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad nauseam means to a sickening degree, repeated until one feels ill.

clue.text: Could be active, say

definitions.meaning: active is one grammatical form of a verb, beside passive
to say is to express or articulate

explanation.surface: Something might be lively, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, active and passive are the two voices of a verb; to voice an opinion is to say it.

clue.text: Pay about 60% extra for dance

indicators.note: about means the word for pay goes around the selected letters

parts.note: to foot a bill is to pay it

indicators.note: 60% of the five letters of extra is three letters, its middle ones

explanation.surface: Settle a bill with a sixty per cent surcharge for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: '60%' of a five-letter word is three letters, here the three in the middle; to 'foot' the bill is to pay it.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxtrot is a ballroom dance in slow and quick steps.

clue.text: Man, concealing weapon in clothing

indicators.note: concealing means the word for man hides the weapon inside itself

parts.note: a gent is a man
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A man hides a gun in his clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment is an item of dress, one piece of what someone wears.
